prompt:
PlanRulesCreate and PlanRulesOut (mealie/schema/meal_plan/plan_rules.py) and CreateCookBook and ReadCookBook (mealie/schema/cookbook/cookbook.py) each carry their own copy of the same two validators:
- validate_query_filter_string (on PlanRulesCreate and CreateCookBook): check that a query filter string builds a valid recipe query, and raise ValueError("Invalid query filter string") when it does not;
- validate_query_filter (on PlanRulesOut and ReadCookBook): build the QueryFilterJSON for the stored query_filter_string, logging and returning an empty QueryFilterJSON when it cannot be built.

Put each piece of logic in one place that both schemas use, so that a change to it is made once. This is a refactor: behavior must not change. The four schema classes keep the same fields, the same validation results and the same errors, and every existing test still passes.

Tests: `python -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests` (the whole backend suite). For quicker loops while you work, tests/unit_tests and tests/integration_tests/user_household_tests cover these schemas.
title: One home for the query-filter validation of meal-plan rules and cookbooks
